reasoning_traces.think:
The CPOE persistence falsifier operates by evaluating whether team-level completion percentage over expectation (cpoe) in one season predicts outcomes in the next. It applies four tests: leakage (no lookahead), shuffle (effect survives randomization), split (consistency across halves), and multiplicity (growth in signal strength). Only the leakage test passes, while shuffle and multiplicity fail. The shuffle test rejects the original effect (-0.013) because 87 out of 200 permutations exceed the 95th percentile, indicating no statistical significance. Multiplicity fails due to exponential decay in effective process (logM = -280.842), implying no growth in signal strength. The model probability is derived from z-scoring prior-season cpoe against current season mean, but this fails to generate predictive power post-shuffle. Market probability is derived from devigged spread lines, which remain stable and do not support any exploitable edge. The overall verdict is that the signal is killed, not starved, as sample size (n=4172) exceeds minimum threshold. This demonstrates that season-mean cpoe does not persist strongly enough to produce falsifiable predictive residuals versus closing spread.
